questions.question: You need to create a storage account for SMB file shares that require consistently low latency. Which account configuration should you use?

options.text: Premium performance with the file shares account type (FileStorage)
options.why: Correct. Premium file shares run on SSD and provide predictable low latency.

options.text: Standard performance, general-purpose v2, Cool access tier
options.why: Standard shares are HDD based, and the Cool tier is for infrequent access.

options.text: Premium performance with the block blobs account type
options.why: Premium block blob accounts do not host file shares.

options.text: Standard performance with a hierarchical namespace
options.why: A hierarchical namespace is for Data Lake Storage, not low-latency SMB shares.

questions.explanation: Premium FileStorage accounts host SSD-backed file shares and are the only accounts that support NFS shares.

questions.question: Your company requires a second layer of encryption for all data in a storage account that already exists. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new storage account with infrastructure encryption enabled and move the data
options.why: Correct. Infrastructure encryption can be enabled only when the account is created.

options.text: Enable infrastructure encryption on the existing account
options.why: This setting cannot be changed after creation.

options.text: Switch the existing account to a customer-managed key
options.why: A customer-managed key changes who controls the key, not the number of encryption layers.

options.text: Enable secure transfer required
options.why: Secure transfer protects data in transit, not at rest.

questions.explanation: Infrastructure encryption adds a second AES-256 layer and must be chosen at creation time.

questions.question: You plan to configure a storage account to use a customer-managed key stored in Azure Key Vault. Which two requirements must be met? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: The key vault has soft delete and purge protection enabled
options.why: Correct. Azure Storage requires both on the vault that holds the key.

options.text: The storage account has a managed identity with permission to wrap and unwrap the key
options.why: Correct. For example, the Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User role.

options.text: The storage account uses the Premium performance tier
options.why: Customer-managed keys are supported on standard and premium accounts.

options.text: The storage account firewall is set to Allow
options.why: Network settings do not determine whether a customer-managed key can be used.

questions.explanation: The account uses its managed identity to reach the key, and purge protection prevents the key from being destroyed permanently by mistake.

questions.question: A storage account uses a customer-managed key. A security administrator disables the key in Azure Key Vault. What is the effect?

options.text: Requests to read or write data in the account fail until access to the key is restored
options.why: Correct. Storage cannot unwrap the data encryption key without the customer-managed key.

options.text: The account switches to Microsoft-managed keys automatically
options.why: Storage does not fall back to Microsoft-managed keys.

options.text: Existing data is deleted
options.why: The data remains, encrypted, and becomes available again when the key is re-enabled.

options.text: Only new data is affected
options.why: Reads of existing data also fail.

questions.explanation: Control over the key, including the ability to revoke access, is the purpose of a customer-managed key.

questions.question: You must create a storage account with the following requirements: only HTTPS requests are accepted, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are refused, and no container can be made public. Which Azure CLI parameters should you include?

options.text: --https-only true --min-tls-version TLS1_2 --allow-blob-public-access false
options.why: Correct. These parameters enforce secure transfer, TLS 1.2 and block anonymous access.

options.text: --default-action Deny --bypass None
options.why: These parameters configure the firewall, not transport security or anonymous access.

options.text: --require-infrastructure-encryption --sku Premium_LRS
options.why: These parameters affect encryption layers and performance.

options.text: --allow-shared-key-access false --kind BlobStorage
options.why: These parameters disable key access and choose a legacy account kind.

questions.explanation: Secure transfer, minimum TLS version and anonymous access are separate account properties that can be set at creation.
